biography:
Steve White Trio is a UK acid jazz and jazz pop ensemble led by the legendary drummer Steve White, renowned for his foundational role in The Style Council during the 1980s and his appearances at Live Aid in 1985. White first gained fame playing with Paul Weller at age 17, becoming a permanent member of The Style Council and contributing to hits like "Long Hot Summer" and major solo albums including Stanley Road and Heavy Soul. Beyond his work with Weller, White co-founded The Jazz Renegades, one of the pioneering bands of the Acid Jazz movement, and has performed with notable artists such as The Young Disciples, Galliano, JTQ, Oasis, and The Who. His musical journey also includes collaborations in groups like Trio Valore, The Players, and The Family Silver, showcasing his versatility across jazz, soul, and rock genres.

The Steve White Trio, featuring long-time collaborator Chris Hague on guitar and Joel White on keyboards, marks White’s debut as a bandleader with the album Soul Drums, released on March 20, 2026, under Acid Jazz Records as part of the new "Jazz Sessions" series. The instrumental record pays tribute to White’s jazz roots and filmic influences, blending sixties Hammond organ-led R&B, funk grooves, and soul textures inspired by Graham Bond and Brian Auger. The album includes a reworking of The Style Council’s "My Ever Changing Moods" and the single "Changes," reflecting White’s cinematic approach to composition. With a mid-century inspired sleeve and a lineup that also features saxophonist Steve Beighton on select tracks, Soul Drums celebrates White’s enduring legacy while introducing his new trio to the acid jazz scene.

The trio has embarked on a UK tour in April and May 2026, performing at venues such as Band on the Wall in Manchester, Slay in Glasgow, and Thekla in Bristol, with Matt Deighton providing support on most dates. Their music fuses sixties Hammond soul, funk, and blues with a subtle jazz edge, creating a distinctive sound that honors White’s past while pushing forward into new creative territory. As a drum master and legend of acid jazz, Steve White continues to shape the genre through this trio, blending his rich history with fresh, melodic, and cinematic compositions that resonate with both longtime fans and new audiences.
